newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.06 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.06 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.06 percent to close at 1.0681 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank lowered the reais-dollar mini-band, dealers said.
The Central Bank depreciated the mini-band Tuesday for the fourth time this month, lowering it 0.09 percent to between 1.0680 and 1.0730 reais per dollar through a buy/sell auction.

The previous mini-band was set on Thursday at between 1.0670 and 1.0720 per greenback. So far this month, the mini-band has fallen 0.42 percent against the dollar compared with an average drop of between 0.57 and 0.61 percent in the past four months.
In late afternoon, the Central Bank bought dollars at 1.0680 reais per greenback to drain the excess of dollars from the market.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real dropped 0.03 percent to end at 1.0733 per dollar.
In the parallel market, the real closed steady at 1.130 per greenback.
